runs.title: Surface failures are current; broad model decline remains unproven
runs.summary: A fresh public-source review found active ChatGPT upload and image failures, a resolved 3 September outage cluster, narrow Grok gibberish reports, and task-level complaints that remain confounded.

runs.title: Incidents resolved; rollout and route changes still make quality hard to generalize
runs.summary: The latest provider checks are operational, while official model changes, a nominal scoped coding tracker, current leaderboards, and mixed task reports sharpen the distinction between reliability, routing, field outcomes, and broad capability.

runs.title: The newest lead is a route, not a model collapse
runs.summary: Provider documentation makes fallback and allowance confounders explicit; a technically detailed but unconfirmed Gemini route report sharpens the next test; scoped trackers still do not prove broad capability decline.

runs.title: Astra/Codex has an incident cluster; core decline remains unproven
runs.summary: Fresh open Codex reports add a detailed Astra agent-behavior, safety, orchestration, and quota incident cluster. Aggregate status and rolling field outcomes remain counterweights, so the verdict narrows to a real user-facing incident without proving core capability regression.

runs.title: Astra is not broadly worse; the system around it is failing in public
runs.summary: OpenAI confirmed a recent usage-limit incident, a fresh desktop transport report separates web from client behavior, and a current Project-link incident adds product context. The field panel remains strong but costly and rolling, so the verdict stays narrow: specific surfaces are different, blocked, or expensive; broad capability decline is unproven.

runs.title: One narrow Gemini tool-use regression joins the ledger; broad decline remains unproven
runs.summary: A repeated matched-context Gemini report adds the strongest capability-shaped lead yet, while Claude status and new Astra/Codex cost and transport evidence show why usable access and capability must stay separate. Independent replication and server-side attribution remain open.

runs.title: A tool call can fail without the model getting dumber
runs.summary: Fresh reports add a quoted backend explanation for a Gemini Deep Research MCP failure, a repeated Gemini Agentic Video tool-loop failure, and controlled Codex runtime evidence of faster allowance consumption. Claude Cowork remains the current degraded component, while no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.

runs.title: Astra has a narrow monitorability regression; broad decline remains unproven
runs.summary: OpenAI documents lower Astra monitorability than Sol and warns that accumulated context can change follow-through. New Codex reports add intent drift and a sharp weekly-meter discontinuity, while Terminal-Bench supplies a cross-sectional performance counterweight; current status pages still point to a Claude Cowork surface issue rather than a broad model decline.

runs.title: Astra is mixed on benchmarks; the work system still breaks around it
runs.summary: Artificial Analysis adds a real negative work slice beside Astra’s benchmark gains, Astra-26 shows tool-stack sensitivity, and current Codex reports add capacity, session, tool, and allowance failures. No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.

runs.title: The quota problem is not Astra-only
runs.summary: Fresh OpenAI status incidents and a Sol control show a broken or expensive work system more clearly than a broad capability decline; model-quality evidence remains mixed and scoped.

runs.title: A capacity-conditioned Astra drop is a lead, not a weight verdict
runs.summary: An open same-task Codex report sharpens a narrow Astra capacity/serving-quality lead, while missing served-model provenance and cross-model cached-context telemetry keep broad capability decline unproven.

runs.title: The work window is the product
runs.summary: A quantified allowance-drain report makes usable access and economics the freshest lead; provider rules, surface failures, safety disclosures, benchmarks, and community counterreports keep broad capability decline unproven.

runs.title: The watch needs an alert contract
runs.summary: Current provider status pages are calm, but a historical Anthropic postmortem, NIST evaluation guidance, Google SRE alert rules, and fresh community intake language sharpen the distinction between user-visible symptoms, serving causes, and broad capability decline.

runs.title: The budget is part of the truth
runs.summary: A detailed Codex task exposes a missing task-wide budget and stop receipt; fresh access and entitlement reports block quality judgment, a Gemini URL-input path recovers, and community and observability signals sharpen the decision receipt without proving broad capability decline.

runs.title: The system changed; “worse” still needs a controlled receipt
runs.summary: OpenAI’s incident history and Google’s Antigravity tool-contract change add concrete service and product lanes; Anthropic’s internal success counterweight, competing public drift monitors, and current Codex switching reports keep broad capability decline unproven.

runs.title: Drift is measurable; the cause still needs a receipt
runs.summary: A repeated-measurement monitor makes temporal movement a real signal, while a narrow GPT-5.6 Sol session report and judge-reliability evidence sharpen the replay requirement; current status pages and source limits keep broad capability decline unproven.

runs.title: An outage and a surface split; broad decline still needs a test
runs.summary: A resolved Claude multi-model incident adds current availability evidence. OpenAI’s Chat-only Sol update makes surface identity explicit, while community access and Chat-versus-Work reports and judge-instability research sharpen the next replay without proving broad capability decline.

runs.title: A resolved outage, a route lead, and no broad decline
runs.summary: OpenAI had a resolved ChatGPT Conversations incident. A detailed same-account Chat-versus-Work report supplies a narrow execution-class lead, while routing and capacity reports remain unverified and RoboDojo provides a positive cross-sectional counterweight.

runs.title: The rollout moved before the verdict did
runs.summary: OpenAI placed GPT-6 Sol and Luna in Work, Codex, and the API but not ordinary Chat, while Work and Claude recorded resolved incidents. A client/server model-attribution mismatch, hidden conversation-capacity reports, and a positive Opus 5.5 counterweight sharpen the surface and provenance diagnosis without proving broad capability decline.

runs.title: Independent tests disagree on the GPT-6 verdict
runs.summary: Sonar and PolicyBench put GPT-6 Sol above GPT-5.6 Sol on their suites, while a matched ten-task Luna comparison gives the older model better quality judgments. A Codex/API effort mismatch and recent status and pricing records keep route, budget, and access explanations live.

runs.title: A negative coding slice, a near-tie, and a real outage
runs.summary: Bug Hunt's fresh coding slice is negative for GPT-6 Sol, Braintrust's 175-task API suite is nearly tied, and OpenAI records a resolved Codex outage; the mixed estimands keep broad decline unproven.

runs.title: RoboHarm reports a safety gap; it does not show model degradation
runs.summary: RoboHarm compares safety refusals and task completion across embodied robot policies, not model versions over time. A negative coding slice, a near-tied API result, and the resolved Codex outage keep the broad-decline verdict unproven.

runs.title: Opus 5.5 drew “Claude is back” reports. That is not a recovery test.
runs.summary: Opus 5.5 adds positive provider, selected-task, and user-reaction evidence after a version change; none is a test of decline and recovery, and broad model degradation remains unproven.

runs.title: GPT-6.1 Astra held after reported safety test failure
runs.summary: OpenAI’s reported GPT-6.1 release hold adds a predeployment safety signal. A separate Claude Code file-loss account remains unverified. Neither establishes broad degradation among deployed popular models.

runs.title: ChatGPT and Claude had separate service incidents on 29 September
runs.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI published separate 29 September service incidents. The latest OpenAI 30 September status updates said two affected surfaces had recovered. Neither establishes broad deployed-model capability decline.

runs.title: Space Pages still showed degraded status after a recovery notice. Model decline is separate.
runs.summary: OpenAI’s Space Pages incident remained degraded/monitoring after a later 30 September mitigation update; Anthropic reported no incident. An Opus 5.5 longitudinal suite was still collecting baseline, so broad deployed-model decline remains unproven.

runs.title: Space Pages recovered; Opus 5.5 sentiment fell, but no task verdict is ready
runs.summary: OpenAI marked Space Pages recovered while the Opus 5.5 task series remains in baseline. Reddit sentiment and opposing user accounts do not establish a model-quality decline.

runs.title: Opus 5.5 scored 94.2% on BridgeBench; a decline is not established
runs.summary: BridgeBench’s 2 October composite score is inside its stated variance band and combines task score, tokens, and cost. LiveNerf has no post-baseline result, and current status pages show no declared service incident.

runs.title: LiveNerf has completed its baseline; no comparison result is ready
runs.summary: The 10-day baseline is complete, but its post-baseline series has no result yet. Marginlab also says Opus 5.5 detection is paused during baseline collection; the broad decline verdict remains unestablished.

runs.title: OpenAI reports a Work Mode incident; Opus 5.5 regression remains unproven
runs.summary: OpenAI reports a Work Mode incident mitigated under monitoring; Anthropic documents model fallbacks for some requests. BridgeBench’s Opus 5.5 score rose from its 2 October low, LiveNerf has no comparison result, and one user’s matched-prompt report remains unverified.

runs.title: OpenAI marked incidents recovered; one GPT-5.6 quality report has no replay data
runs.summary: OpenAI marked several service incidents recovered and showed all systems operational at check time. A same-day user complaint lacks task and served-model evidence, so broad degradation remains unproven; the report gives a status-first replay action.

runs.title: OpenAI resolves a Work desktop issue and a separate Agent response issue
runs.summary: Two reported product issues were marked resolved. No broad model decline is established; the GPT-5.6 complaint lacks a matched replay, and LiveNerf's pending comparison needs a windowing fix check.

runs.title: One Opus 5.5 report shows higher token use; cause unresolved
runs.summary: A single-user issue reports increased Opus 5.5 thinking and output tokens after 1 October, when Claude Code also changed version. Recent OpenAI error incidents were marked recovered; LiveNerf has no comparison result.

runs.title: Opus 5.5 reports now include a server-delivered prompt change
runs.summary: Issue comments describe different 1 October client and prompt histories, including a reported server-delivered prompt experiment. These reports remain uncontrolled; no broad capability decline or confirmed core-model regression is established.

runs.title: One Opus 5.5 report describes 17 unrequested edits. It is not a model test.
runs.summary: A 4 October commenter reports costly agent configuration overreach in a highly customized, model-switching session. This is one unverified user incident, not a controlled core-model regression result; safety and rollback steps are now explicit.

runs.title: Gemini changed model access; a broad model decline is not established
runs.summary: Google documented a staged tier-based access change while separate reports describe an 8 October outage and Pro app failures. Those product and service signals do not establish a core-model decline.

runs.title: OpenAI reports GPT-6.1 Sol Codex/Work performance issue; broad decline remains unestablished
runs.summary: Provider-declared degraded performance is under monitoring. Public account and replay reports add narrow leads; one cross-sectional comparison is mixed. No broad capability decline is established.
